transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-06-21 | Time: 15:00 UTC | Duration: 48 mins
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Rajesh Singh (LumenForge Head of Partnerships), Emily Park (Cloud Product), Tom Bennett (Infra Lead)

Summary (auto): Intro & discovery for potential partnership. Quick product overview from Redwood, LumenForge capabilities, and high-level integration + go-to-market discussion. Left with action items to run benchmarks and exchange security docs.

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya, AE at Redwood Inference — joining me is Diego Alvarez, our solutions engineer. Quick roll call?
[00:08] Rajesh Singh: Hey Maya, Rajesh here. Emily and Tom are with me, thanks for setting this up.
[00:12] Emily Park: Hi all.
[00:13] Tom Bennett: Tom here.
[00:14] Diego Alvarez: Awesome. I'll do a super high-level SE intro later, but today we want to understand LumenForge's partner goals and what technical integration would look like.
[00:22] Rajesh Singh: Yeah, we're exploring a couple routes — reseller partnership for our enterprise customers and offering managed infra for inference workloads. We have a few customers asking for turnkey LLM inference on private clouds.
[00:33] Maya Chen: Perfect. Very aligned. To start, can you maybe describe your typical customer profile and what they'd expect from a partner like Redwood?
[00:41] Rajesh Singh: Sure. Most customers are mid to large financial and media companies — heavy on compliance. They want predictable latency, multi-region, and options for on-prem or VPC. Cost matters but security is often the gating factor.
[00:54] Emily Park: And our differentiator is we package infra + ops — if Redwood can plug into that flow we'd sell that as an add-on.
[01:02] Diego Alvarez: Understood. From a tech perspective, do you have a preferred model family or GPU spec you plan to offer to customers? A100, H100, or mixed?
[01:11] Tom Bennett: We're primarily investing in H100 for new clusters, but we still operate A100 fleets. NVLink topology is a thing for some customers who need large-model inference.
[01:21] Maya Chen: Great. Redwood supports multiple variants; our dedicated offering can be pinned to specific GPU types. One note: when customers talk about NVLink and multi-GPU behind a single model, that usually pushes into a private or dedicated deployment rather than simple hosted.
[01:34] Rajesh Singh: Makes sense. For the reseller motion, commercial questions: margin, co-selling, lead routing — do you have a partner program outline to share?
[01:43] Maya Chen: Yes. I'll share our partner playbook after the call — it has commercial tiers, referral vs reseller terms, and partner enablement.
[01:49] Diego Alvarez: On the technical front, for benchmarks we typically run a small eval harness — sequence length, batch sizes, concurrency — to map throughput and per-token cost. Would you want Redwood to run benchmarks on your H100 clusters or run them in our hosted infra for comparison?
[02:05] Tom Bennett: Ideally both. We want to show customers that LumenForge-managed H100 can match or beat hosted per-token latency at scale.
[02:12] Emily Park: Also need to validate warm-start latency with KV cache, because many of our workloads are chatty and reuse prefixes.
[02:19] Diego Alvarez: Totally, KV cache behavior is critical. Our runtime supports prefix caching and automatic reuse, which helps latency on repeated contexts. Quick caveat: some of those features interact with model quantization choices.
[02:31] Rajesh Singh: On security, customers will ask for SOC2 / ISO, egress controls, SSO, audit logs. Do you have a standard security pack?
[02:40] Maya Chen: Yes — SOC2 Type II, ISO attestations, and an enterprise security pack including network diagrams, KMS/HSM integration notes, and SSO/SAML guides. I'll drop those docs in the playbook link.
[02:50] Tom Bennett: About KMS — do you integrate with customer-managed KMS or only Redwood-managed? For private deployments we need to bring our own keys.
[02:58] Diego Alvarez: We support both: Redwood Private can be configured with customer KMS/HSM and bring-your-own-key. For hosted, there's a managed KMS option with customer key escrow available for enterprise.
[03:09] Rajesh Singh: Good. For private deployments, what's the control plane topology? We have cases where customers are air-gapped or require no external callouts.
[03:17] Maya Chen: There are two models: 1) VPC with a customer-managed control plane and a network peering option, and 2) fully on-prem package that runs in air-gapped environments — we call that Redwood Private. Both support audit logging and RBAC.
[03:29] Emily Park: Pricing question: do you have committed tiers for Dedicated? Some of our customers want predictable monthly billing.
[03:36] Maya Chen: Yes. Dedicated is reserved capacity with monthly/annual commits and predictable throughput pricing. We can share example commitment tiers in the playbook.
[03:43] Diego Alvarez: For the benchmark we should align on the target SLOs: p50/p95 latencies, tokens-per-second, and cost per 1k tokens. That way the comparison is apples-to-apples.
[03:53] Tom Bennett: We'll provide target SLOs and sample prompts. Expect a mix of 1k-2k token sequences and some 4k sequences for longform summarization.
[04:01] Rajesh Singh: Regarding go-to-market, how do you prefer to handle co-branded materials and customer references?
[04:07] Maya Chen: We usually offer a co-marketing package for certified partners — joint case studies, webinars, and listing in our partner catalog. Terms in the playbook.
[04:13] Emily Park: Operational question: if we run Redwood runtime on our clusters, who handles upgrades and kernel optimizations? That's important for perf.
[04:21] Diego Alvarez: If it's Redwood-managed within Dedicated or Private, we operate the runtime and push validated kernel updates. For reseller-managed infra where you operate the stack, we provide validated releases and an upgrade guide; we can also offer a managed ops add-on.
[04:35] Rajesh Singh: A couple of technical clarifications: 1) model weights residency — do we store weights on local NVMe or on NFS? 2) How do you handle quantized models?
[04:44] Diego Alvarez: We typically store weights on local NVMe for latency-sensitive paths. For quantization, we support int8/4-bit workflows; some model families get better latency gains than others. There's a tradeoff in quality but we provide recommendations per workload.
[04:58] Maya Chen: (brief) Also mention fallback policies: if a large model isn't available, Redwood can route to a compatible smaller variant to preserve uptime — useful for managed customers.
[05:06] Tom Bennett: Nice. For networking, we need specifics: port ranges, egress endpoints, and whether the control plane needs outbound HTTPS. Some customers block outbound traffic.
[05:16] Diego Alvarez: We have an air-gapped on-prem option but for VPC deployments the control plane needs HTTPS outbound to coordinate rollouts and metrics; that can be optional if you run the full private control plane. We'll share a network diagram.
[05:28] Rajesh Singh: Any red flags or limitations we should be aware of?
[05:31] Diego Alvarez: Major limits depend on model size and multi-GPU scaling; cross-node NVLink for distributed inference has complexity and is generally recommended for very large sparse or retrieval-augmented models. Otherwise, the runtime handles continuous batching and KV cache gracefully.
[05:45] Maya Chen: To make this concrete, proposed next tactical steps: share playbook and security pack; schedule a 90-min technical deep dive where Diego runs through architecture and we schedule a benchmark slot on H100; LumenForge to share workloads and topology.
[05:58] Rajesh Singh: Agreed. One more thing — channel economics: do you have a standard discount for partner resale?
[06:04] Maya Chen: We have tiered margins based on commitment and enablement level. I'll include tier examples.
[06:08] Emily Park: For the benchmark instrumentation, we want logs and traces to feed into our console to show customers. Is there a way to stream observability data into LumenForge dashboards?
[06:18] Diego Alvarez: We export metrics and traces via OpenTelemetry and have webhooks for events. We can also provide a dashboard URL for demo purposes.
[06:26] Tom Bennett: Good. On compliance, some customers need SLA-backed data residency. Do you support region pinning for data and model hosting?
[06:33] Maya Chen: Yes — region pinning and tenant isolation are supported in Dedicated and Private deployments.
[06:38] Rajesh Singh: Wonderful. Any immediate blockers for taking this forward?
[06:42] Maya Chen: Not from our side. We'll circulate documents and propose a technical deep dive timeslot next week.
[06:47] Emily Park: We'll sync internally and pick dates.
[06:49] [crosstalk]
[06:50] Rajesh Singh: One last micro detail — for customers that want to white-label, is that possible?
[06:55] Maya Chen: We have co-branded options and a reseller license. We'll include that in the playbook.
[06:59] Diego Alvarez: Alright, unless there are more questions, we'll recap.
[07:02] Rajesh Singh: No more from me, thanks.

Recap / Next steps (auto):
- Redwood to share partner playbook, partner tiers, and security pack (Maya)

References shared: partner playbook (link to be sent), security pack (SOC2/ISO), proposed benchmark spreadsheet (will be shared by Diego).
